01 / MEMEBASE

Meme coins. COINx pairs.

Memebase is a Solana interface for launching meme coins on Pump. Every new Memebase launch uses COINx as its quote asset. Choose an image, name and ticker, then approve the launch in your wallet.

Memebase is an independent application. The name and pixel artwork do not imply affiliation with Coinbase, xStocks or Pump.

Launch a coin

  1. Upload a PNG, JPG or WebP image, up to 256 KB. Enter a name, ticker and description.
  2. Add optional X and website links. These are saved with the token identity and referenced by mint-specific, content-addressed metadata.
  3. Optionally enter a developer buy in COINx. Leave it blank for no initial purchase.
  4. Select Launch token. Connect your Solana wallet and sign the ownership message if prompted.
  5. Review and sign the Pump creation transaction in your wallet. An optional developer buy is included in that same transaction.

You need SOL for account creation and network fees, plus COINx for an optional developer buy. The buy amount is a spending cap; the Pump instruction may spend less. No separate liquidity deposit or 50% developer-buy split is charged.

New tokens use Pump’s Token-2022 creation flow, six token decimals and Pump’s standard supply. Mayhem mode and holder rewards are disabled. The saved image and links cannot be edited through Memebase. Token metadata is served by this website, not permanent decentralized storage.

After submission, wait for finality. Reopen the token page to resume confirmation. An expired preparation is reconciled on mainnet before a new mint is prepared.

Why COINx?

COINx is the quote asset for new launches. Token prices, market caps, reserves and indexed volume are expressed in COINx, rather than USDC or SOL.

COINx mint · Solana mainnet

Xs7ZdzSHLU9ftNJsii5fCeJhoRWSC32SQGzGQtePxNu

This quote is listed in Pump’s quote-control configuration and uses the Token-2022 program with eight decimals. Memebase verifies the mint and quote eligibility when preparing a launch.

COINx is a tokenized equity asset associated with Coinbase stock; it is not USDC, a dollar stablecoin or native Base ETH. Its value can move. A COINx pairing does not stabilize the launched token. Use the mint address to identify the asset.

Legacy BlueMint tokens keep their original on-chain USDC pools and metadata, but their listings have been retired from Memebase. Their USDC fee claims remain separate. New Memebase listings use COINx.

Pump fees

New Pump launches use Pump’s on-chain trading fee schedule. Memebase adds no separate trading fee. The former 1.25% Raydium platform fee and 40% / 60% allocation do not apply to Pump launches.

The wallet that launches the coin is set as its Pump creator. Any creator fees accrue under Pump’s rules. Connect that wallet to Pump’s fee interface to inspect and claim eligible balances. COINx, USDC and SOL receipts are different assets.

Legacy USDC claims

Existing BlueMint LaunchLab pools retain their original 1.25% platform fee and zero creator fee. Legacy claims still go to the configured BlueMint treasury. These balances are separate from Pump creator fees.

Legacy USDC claims

Creator wallet & treasury

New Pump launches do not send creator fees or developer buys to a Memebase treasury. Your wallet signs creation, pays rent and receives tokens from an optional buy. Pump manages its protocol and creator fee accounts.

The legacy USDC treasury remains 85a8ERAhk1ZPYyGwj4zkjVKZdfqaEUcSpTt9GCz5xA7j. That address and the deployed USDC vault are retained for existing BlueMint markets. They are not a COINx buyback engine.

Pump curve → PumpSwap

Trading starts on Pump’s bonding curve. Purchases add quote reserves and release tokens; sales move in the opposite direction. Pump determines the curve parameters and graduation conditions.

When a curve completes, Pump’s migration process creates its canonical PumpSwap market. A short interval can occur between curve completion and pool availability. Memebase checks the canonical pool and verified vault balances after migration.

No automatic Memebase COINx buyback, liquidity reinvestment, holder rewards or price floor is enabled. The legacy USDC keeper only services eligible, approved legacy markets.

Charts & trading

Token pages show verified, finalized on-chain reserve observations. Candles group these observations and available indexed curve trades into one-minute intervals. Market cap is quote price multiplied by token supply. Reserves show the actual quote balance available to the market, excluding identifiable pool fees.

A ≥ before volume means partial indexed history. An unavailable volume is shown as Indexing rather than zero. Historical candles may fill in after the first observation. New finalized trades are indexed through per-coin subscriptions on the curve and PumpSwap. HTTP history backfill is bounded and reconnects can leave gaps, so volume is marked as indexed and may be partial. King of Memes ranks new Memebase COINx coins by indexed quote volume in the rolling last five minutes; legacy USDC markets are excluded. A coin needs positive recent volume to hold the crown.

Use Trade on Pump on the token page to trade with Pump’s interface. Availability in Axiom or another terminal depends on that service’s support for COINx quote pairs and indexing; Memebase cannot force terminal support.

Every finalized token keeps a page at /token/<mint-address>. Legacy on-chain markets keep their original mint and pool addresses; their Memebase listings have been retired.

Check readiness

Launch preparation checks Solana mainnet, approved COINx configuration, token-program ownership and transaction simulation. Your wallet must sign before anything is broadcast. A preparation passing simulation does not guarantee a future transaction will succeed.
